correctness.rationale: Reconstructing all basis-pair Rota–Baxter equations produces exactly nine explicit polynomials. Their square relations force h=j=0 in the radical; the remaining determinant polynomial is geometrically irreducible, so the radical is prime. Its Jacobian proves the smoothness dichotomy. Determinant-fiber stratification gives the precise Grothendieck classes and all finite-field counts. A nonzero-weight dual-number solution with j=epsilon has no second-order lift because j squared is an exact defining equation. A symbolic verifier and full ambient enumerations over F2 and F3 independently replay the arithmetic.

value.rationale: Rota–Baxter operators are naturally a polynomial moduli problem. The precise distinction between field-valued classifications and the unreduced deformation functor is structural: a full moduli scheme can be nonsmooth/nonreduced even when its reduction is smooth. The explicit first-order obstruction makes that distinction operational, while the weight-dependent Grothendieck and finite-field counts show a genuine arithmetic and geometric bifurcation for the exact same algebra. This resolves a natural intrinsic invariant not supplied by the source operator tables.
